summary.intent: Diagnose and fix an intermittent CI failure (`expected [] to deeply equal ['Button']`) in the napi worker-threads integration test, and handle the subagent's hand-back report on it.
summary.outcome: The flake was traced to a test-fixture race, not a product bug. A test-only fix (commit dd23c82d, PR #368, trail #231) gives the worker test its own temp `Button.tsx`, and 17 non-review checks pass. A separate real race in `dependency_types.rs` was found but left unfixed.

repo: Integration tests use vitest `pool: 'forks'`, so test files run in parallel processes and share `fixtures/src`; tests that mutate shared fixtures can race with other files.

`plugin.integration.test.ts` rewrites the shared `fixtures/src/Button.tsx` in `afterEach` and in two tests. `writeFileSync` truncates first, so a concurrent reader can see an empty file and find no components.
`SESSIONS` is a process-global `DashMap`, each worker has a unique id, and `WatchSession::initialize` is idempotent under the writer lock, so registry and first-extraction races were ruled out.
`just lint` and `build:napi` modify `packages/napi/binding.d.ts`; it must be reverted before committing.
Changes that are test-only need no changeset.
The sandbox blocks the `napi build` step with `spawn EPERM`, so builds and test loops had to run with the sandbox off.
Branches are cut from fresh `origin/main`, linked to a trail with base `main`, and pushed without force.

code.finding: The dependency index is written through a temp file named with only the process id. Workers in one process share that name, so concurrent writers can clobber each other. `cache.rs` avoids this with a sequence number. It affects projects with dependencies, not the dependency-free Button fixture.
The `afterEach` restores the shared Button fixture via `fs.writeFileSync(BUTTON_FIXTURE, original)`, which truncates before writing and is the source of the race.
The test walked the shared `fixtures/src` and failed at the last (`later`) call. It now writes its own `Button.tsx` into a `mkdtemp` directory in `beforeAll` and removes it in `afterAll`.

workflow: Reproducing a flake deterministically (emptying the fixture file) confirmed the root cause more reliably than rate-based loops, which only failed 1 in 100 under CPU load.
Validating a fix needs large repeat counts both plain and under CPU load (200 each here) because the failure rate was so low.
A subagent's hand-back report should be verified independently; the PR state, CI results and diff size were re-checked with a Bash call.
Ruling out hypotheses explicitly (teardown, first extraction, PR 351, path-keyed caches) kept the investigation focused.

friction: The failure was extremely rare (about 1 in 100 under load, 0 in 100 plain), which made reproduction slow.
The sandbox blocks `napi build` with `spawn EPERM`, so builds and test loops had to run with the sandbox off.
`just lint` and `build:napi` modify `binding.d.ts`, which must be manually reverted.
An earlier suspicion that #349's changes caused the flake turned out to be wrong.
The Entire Gates check was still pending when the subagent last checked.
open_items: Fix the temp-file naming race in `dependency_types.rs` (~line 1344) with a unique sequence-based name like `cache.rs`; the assistant offered to start it as its own trail.
#346 still has a red check and stays at risk until #368 merges and #346 picks up the fix.
Merge #368 once the Entire Gates check completes.
The #335/#345 scope follow-up, including a generated-program comparison against TypeScript's checker, is still running.
The `--pool=forks` and threads variants were not run separately.
